summary: Montana's oldest lookout site (tent camp 1907, stone cabin 1910), topped since 1952 by the present L-4 cab, still the only active lookout on the Cabinet Ranger District.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a stone base

access.note: Reached via Big Eddy Trail #998; firelookout.com describes the lookout as available for emergencies rather than a standard rental

visit.trail_note: Big Eddy Trail #998, about 10 miles northwest of Noxon, Sanders County; trailhead/ending elevation 6,167 ft

events.note: First recorded Montana lookout; a tent camp just below the Star/Squaw Peak summit on the then Cabinet National Forest
Stone cabin built below the summit by ranger Granville "Granny" Gordon and wife Pauline; still standing
First L-4 cab, gable-roof model, built on the summit
Present L-4 cab on a stone base built, replacing the 1930 structure; remains the only active lookout on the Cabinet Ranger District
Registered August 20, 1996 as US 178, nominated by Gary Weber, FFLA
Peak renamed from Squaw Peak to Star Peak/Star Mountain

evidence.supports: 1907 tent camp, first lookout in Montana
evidence.quote: In 1907 the first forest lookout on the old Cabinet National Forest (and the State of Montana) camped in a tent just below the summit of Star Peak (formerly Squaw Peak).

evidence.supports: 1952 present L-4 on stone base, only active lookout on district
evidence.quote: The present L-4 on a stone base was built in 1952 and remains the only active lookout on the Cabinet Ranger District.

evidence.supports: NHLR registration 1996, US 178, nominated by Gary Weber FFLA

evidence.supports: 1910 stone cabin built by Granville and Pauline Gordon
evidence.quote: Three years later, Noxon's first ranger, Granville "Granny" Gordon and his wife Pauline built the stone cabin that still stands at the edge of the talus below the existing lookout.

evidence.supports: 1930 first L-4 gable-roof cab, followed by 1952 present L-4
evidence.quote: In 1930, the first L-4 cab, a gable-roof model, was built on the summit, followed by the present L-4 cab in 1952.
The Political Correctness Police renamed the summit Star Mountain in 2004.
Available for emergencies, it is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register.
Known lookout personnel: 1959: Tommy Richards; 1967: Mary Harker.

evidence.supports: trail access via Big Eddy Trail #998, elevation 6167 ft, first recorded lookout site claim
evidence.quote: Big Eddy Trail #998 leads to Star Peak Lookout. Star Peak is the location of the first recorded lookout site in Montana. The original rock house still sits below the current lookout which was built in 1910.

evidence.supports: views of Scotchman Peaks area, Cabinet Mountains Wilderness, and Clark Fork Valley
evidence.quote: Stunning views of the Scotchman Peaks Recommended Wilderness Area, Cabinet Mountains Wilderness, and the Clark Fork Valley can be seen from the peak.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service's Big Eddy Trailhead page says the 'current lookout' was built in 1910, but NHLR and firelookout.com both say the present L-4 cab dates to 1952, with 1910 belonging to the stone cabin below the summit. Treated the FS page's 1910 date as likely referring to the stone cabin, not the active lookout cab, but flagged the discrepancy rather than silently picking one.

notes_for_editor: firelookout.com's phrasing about the 2004 renaming ('Political Correctness Police') was not carried into the story; only the factual rename date was kept. No rental/booking page found for Star Peak specifically, unlike nearby Gem Peak Lookout which does rent through Recreation.gov -- worth a follow-up search if a rental listing matters for this record.
